prompt:
ORDER BY and pagination (LIMIT, OFFSET, FETCH, TOP) that belong to one branch of a set operation (UNION, INTERSECT, EXCEPT) are not kept in that branch, and pagination of the whole set operation is not applied to all of it, when generating dialects that need explicit scoping. A branch's own ORDER BY ... FETCH FIRST must stay with that branch: parenthesised for DuckDB and Postgres, wrapped in SELECT * FROM (...) for SQLite and T-SQL (T-SQL needs an alias and OFFSET 0 ROWS), unchanged for ClickHouse; pagination after the last branch that applies to the whole set operation must wrap it where the dialect requires (e.g. ClickHouse).

For example:

```python
from sqlglot import parse_one, transpile, exp

transpile("SELECT 1 AS x ORDER BY x NULLS FIRST FETCH FIRST 1 ROWS ONLY UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS x", write="duckdb")[0]
# currently: SELECT 1 AS x ORDER BY x NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS x
# expected:  (SELECT 1 AS x ORDER BY x NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1) UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS x

transpile("SELECT 1 AS x ORDER BY x NULLS FIRST FETCH FIRST 1 ROWS ONLY UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS x", write="tsql")[0]
# currently: SELECT 1 AS x ORDER BY x OFFSET 0 ROWS FETCH FIRST 1 ROWS ONLY UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS x
# expected:  SELECT * FROM (SELECT 1 AS x ORDER BY x OFFSET 0 ROWS FETCH FIRST 1 ROWS ONLY) AS _l_0 UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS x

transpile("SELECT 1 AS x ORDER BY x NULLS FIRST FETCH FIRST 1 ROWS ONLY UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS x", write="sqlite")[0]
# currently: SELECT 1 AS x ORDER BY x LIMIT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS x
# expected:  SELECT * FROM (SELECT 1 AS x ORDER BY x LIMIT 1) UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS x

transpile("SELECT * FROM a UNION SELECT * FROM b OFFSET 1", write="clickhouse")[0]
# currently: SELECT * FROM a UNION DISTINCT SELECT * FROM b OFFSET 1
# expected:  SELECT * FROM (SELECT * FROM a UNION DISTINCT SELECT * FROM b) AS _l_0 OFFSET 1
```

ORDER BY and pagination (LIMIT, OFFSET, FETCH, TOP) that belong to one branch of a set operation (UNION, INTERSECT, EXCEPT) are not kept in that branch, and pagination of the whole set operation is not applied to all of it, when generating dialects that need explicit scoping. A branch's own ORDER BY ... FETCH FIRST must stay with that branch: parenthesised for DuckDB and Postgres, wrapped in SELECT * FROM (...) for SQLite and T-SQL (T-SQL needs an alias and OFFSET 0 ROWS), unchanged for ClickHouse; pagination after the last branch that applies to the whole set operation must wrap it where the dialect requires (e.g. ClickHouse).

For example:

```python
from sqlglot import parse_one, transpile, exp

transpile("SELECT 1 AS x ORDER BY x NULLS FIRST FETCH FIRST 1 ROWS ONLY UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS x", write="duckdb")[0]
# currently: SELECT 1 AS x ORDER BY x NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS x
# expected:  (SELECT 1 AS x ORDER BY x NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1) UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS x

transpile("SELECT 1 AS x ORDER BY x NULLS FIRST FETCH FIRST 1 ROWS ONLY UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS x", write="tsql")[0]
# currently: SELECT 1 AS x ORDER BY x OFFSET 0 ROWS FETCH FIRST 1 ROWS ONLY UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS x
# expected:  SELECT * FROM (SELECT 1 AS x ORDER BY x OFFSET 0 ROWS FETCH FIRST 1 ROWS ONLY) AS _l_0 UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS x

transpile("SELECT 1 AS x ORDER BY x NULLS FIRST FETCH FIRST 1 ROWS ONLY UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS x", write="sqlite")[0]
# currently: SELECT 1 AS x ORDER BY x LIMIT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS x
# expected:  SELECT * FROM (SELECT 1 AS x ORDER BY x LIMIT 1) UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS x

transpile("SELECT * FROM a UNION SELECT * FROM b OFFSET 1", write="clickhouse")[0]
# currently: SELECT * FROM a UNION DISTINCT SELECT * FROM b OFFSET 1
# expected:  SELECT * FROM (SELECT * FROM a UNION DISTINCT SELECT * FROM b) AS _l_0 OFFSET 1
```

ORDER BY and pagination (LIMIT, OFFSET, FETCH, TOP) that belong to one branch of a set operation (UNION, INTERSECT, EXCEPT) are not kept in that branch, and pagination of the whole set operation is not applied to all of it, when generating dialects that need explicit scoping. A branch's own ORDER BY ... FETCH FIRST must stay with that branch: parenthesised for DuckDB and Postgres, wrapped in SELECT * FROM (...) for SQLite and T-SQL (T-SQL needs an alias and OFFSET 0 ROWS), unchanged for ClickHouse; pagination after the last branch that applies to the whole set operation must wrap it where the dialect requires (e.g. ClickHouse).

For example:

```python
from sqlglot import parse_one, transpile, exp

transpile("SELECT 1 AS x ORDER BY x NULLS FIRST FETCH FIRST 1 ROWS ONLY UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS x", write="duckdb")[0]
# currently: SELECT 1 AS x ORDER BY x NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS x
# expected:  (SELECT 1 AS x ORDER BY x NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1) UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS x

transpile("SELECT 1 AS x ORDER BY x NULLS FIRST FETCH FIRST 1 ROWS ONLY UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS x", write="tsql")[0]
# currently: SELECT 1 AS x ORDER BY x OFFSET 0 ROWS FETCH FIRST 1 ROWS ONLY UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS x
# expected:  SELECT * FROM (SELECT 1 AS x ORDER BY x OFFSET 0 ROWS FETCH FIRST 1 ROWS ONLY) AS _l_0 UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS x

transpile("SELECT 1 AS x ORDER BY x NULLS FIRST FETCH FIRST 1 ROWS ONLY UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS x", write="sqlite")[0]
# currently: SELECT 1 AS x ORDER BY x LIMIT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS x
# expected:  SELECT * FROM (SELECT 1 AS x ORDER BY x LIMIT 1) UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS x

transpile("SELECT * FROM a UNION SELECT * FROM b OFFSET 1", write="clickhouse")[0]
# currently: SELECT * FROM a UNION DISTINCT SELECT * FROM b OFFSET 1
# expected:  SELECT * FROM (SELECT * FROM a UNION DISTINCT SELECT * FROM b) AS _l_0 OFFSET 1
```

Other forms of the same constructs described above should work as well.

ORDER BY and pagination (LIMIT, OFFSET, FETCH, TOP) that belong to one branch of a set operation (UNION, INTERSECT, EXCEPT) are not kept in that branch, and pagination of the whole set operation is not applied to all of it, when generating dialects that need explicit scoping. A branch's own ORDER BY ... FETCH FIRST must stay with that branch: parenthesised for DuckDB and Postgres, wrapped in SELECT * FROM (...) for SQLite and T-SQL (T-SQL needs an alias and OFFSET 0 ROWS), unchanged for ClickHouse; pagination after the last branch that applies to the whole set operation must wrap it where the dialect requires (e.g. ClickHouse).

For example:

```python
from sqlglot import parse_one, transpile, exp

transpile("SELECT 1 AS x ORDER BY x NULLS FIRST FETCH FIRST 1 ROWS ONLY UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS x", write="duckdb")[0]
# currently: SELECT 1 AS x ORDER BY x NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS x
# expected:  (SELECT 1 AS x ORDER BY x NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1) UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS x

transpile("SELECT 1 AS x ORDER BY x NULLS FIRST FETCH FIRST 1 ROWS ONLY UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS x", write="tsql")[0]
# currently: SELECT 1 AS x ORDER BY x OFFSET 0 ROWS FETCH FIRST 1 ROWS ONLY UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS x
# expected:  SELECT * FROM (SELECT 1 AS x ORDER BY x OFFSET 0 ROWS FETCH FIRST 1 ROWS ONLY) AS _l_0 UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS x

transpile("SELECT 1 AS x ORDER BY x NULLS FIRST FETCH FIRST 1 ROWS ONLY UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS x", write="sqlite")[0]
# currently: SELECT 1 AS x ORDER BY x LIMIT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS x
# expected:  SELECT * FROM (SELECT 1 AS x ORDER BY x LIMIT 1) UNION ALL SELECT 2 AS x

transpile("SELECT * FROM a UNION SELECT * FROM b OFFSET 1", write="clickhouse")[0]
# currently: SELECT * FROM a UNION DISTINCT SELECT * FROM b OFFSET 1
# expected:  SELECT * FROM (SELECT * FROM a UNION DISTINCT SELECT * FROM b) AS _l_0 OFFSET 1
```

Other forms of the same constructs described above should work as well.
